_comment: Hand-kept: what happens next in states with a race not yet called, and each state's recount rule. Every entry was read on the state's own calendar, notice or statute on Nov. 9, 2026 (Tennessee's statute on law.justia.com); `source` is where. Add a date only when an official source gives it, never one worked out by counting days. `offices` limits an entry to those tabs (S, G, H); without it the entry shows wherever the state has a race not yet called. build.py checks the file, drops `source` from the page and prints a note for dates already past: delete those, and a state's entries once its races are called and certified.

dates.text: Last day for a California mail ballot postmarked by Election Day to reach the county and be counted.
Last day for a Mississippi mail ballot postmarked by Election Day to reach the circuit clerk, by 5 p.m. CST, and be counted.
Florida counties running a machine recount must report second unofficial returns by 3 p.m. EST.
Last day to register in person or by mail for Louisiana’s Dec. 12 runoffs.
Last day for military and overseas ballots to reach North Carolina county boards, by 5 p.m. EST.
Last day for Alaska mail ballots sent from within the United States and postmarked by Election Day to arrive and be counted.
Mississippi’s county election commissions must send certified returns to the secretary of state.
North Carolina’s county boards of elections canvass their results at 11 a.m. EST.
Florida counties must file official returns by noon EST.
Florida’s Elections Canvassing Commission meets at 8 a.m. EST to certify the results.
A trailing U.S. House candidate in North Carolina within 1% has until noon EST to demand a recount.
Last day for Alaska ballots mailed from overseas to arrive.
Alaska runs its ranked-choice tabulation for races where no candidate has a majority of first choices.
Minnesota’s State Canvassing Board meets to certify the results.
Last day to register online for Louisiana’s Dec. 12 runoffs.
Maine’s secretary of state must send certified results to the governor.
North Carolina’s State Board of Elections meets at 11 a.m. EST to certify the results.
Washington’s county canvassing boards certify their results.
Alaska’s target date to certify the election. The Division of Elections says the date may change.
California voters have until 5 p.m. PST to fix a missing or mismatched signature on a mail ballot envelope.
Early voting for Louisiana’s runoffs, 8:30 a.m. to 6 p.m. CST each day except Sunday, Nov. 29.
California’s counties must finish their counts and certify results.
Mississippi’s secretary of state must declare the results by this date.
Washington’s secretary of state must certify the results by this date.
California’s secretary of state must certify the statewide results.
Louisiana’s U.S. House runoffs. Polls are open 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. CST.

AK.text: In Alaska a defeated candidate or 10 voters may ask for a recount. The state pays when the gap is 20 votes or fewer, or less than 0.5% of the two candidates’ combined votes.

CA.text: California has no automatic recount. Any voter may ask for one and pays its cost.

FL.text: Florida orders a machine recount when the first unofficial returns show a gap of 0.5% of the votes cast or less, unless the trailing candidate declines in writing.

ME.text: Maine has no automatic recount. A trailing candidate may ask for one, and pays no deposit when the gap is 1% of the votes cast or less, or 1,000 votes or fewer, whichever is less.

MN.text: Minnesota pays for a recount of a U.S. House race when the gap is under 0.25% of the votes and the trailing candidate asks in writing. It is not automatic.

NC.text: In North Carolina a trailing candidate may demand a recount when the gap is 1% of the votes cast or less in a U.S. House race, or 0.5% or 10,000 votes, whichever is less, in a statewide race.

TN.text: Tennessee has no recount on request. Only a court or the body hearing an election contest may order one.

WA.text: Washington requires a machine recount when the gap is under 2,000 votes and under 0.5% of the two candidates’ votes.
